core.title: Give plan artifacts stable URN-based names matching the registered grammar
core.given: A plan artifact (the concrete kinds that play the plan-artifact role come from the stack's structure profile; the list of kinds is not exhaustive)
core.when: you author, name, review or change it — or it simply exists in the repository
core.then: The artifact carries a stable URN-based name that matches the registered grammar and stays constant across renames/refactors.
prefer: Look up the repository's registered naming grammar before naming, build the name as a URN from it (a stable_name), and check the name parses against that grammar.
Keep the same URN when the artifact is renamed, moved or refactored.
avoid: Free-form or ad-hoc names that do not match the registered grammar.
Changing an artifact's URN as part of a rename or refactor.
core.why: The convention defines a stable_name as URN-based, constant across renames/refactors and conforming to the registered grammar; plan artifacts must carry such a name.
evidence: Each plan artifact's name is URN-based and parses against the registered naming grammar.
Plan artifact URNs are unchanged across rename/refactor diffs.
verification: Term stable_name: a URN-based artifact name that stays constant across renames/refactors and matches the registered grammar.

Applicability is gated solely by the plan-artifact role: being a plan artifact is sufficient (new or existing, compliant or not), independent of any operation event, author or phase. Recognizing a file or record as a plan artifact requires an observer that does not exist yet (needs_new_observer); violation findings are verifier outputs, not activation prerequisites.

A review of an in-scope plan artifact can report three violation classes: the name is not URN-based; the name does not match the registered grammar; the artifact's URN changed across a rename/refactor (this comparison requires the prior URN). The name is parsed against the repository's registered naming grammar; neither the rule nor its core defines that grammar's concrete shapes or the syntax by which an artifact declares its URN — those are whatever the repository's own registry declares. Absence of findings means the rule is satisfied, not that it does not apply.

fires: A new plan artifact is created with a correctly formed URN-based name (rule applies; it is satisfied).
A new plan artifact is created with a free-form name.
An existing plan artifact is renamed, moved or refactored and its URN stays unchanged (rule applies; it is satisfied).
An existing plan artifact is renamed or refactored and its URN changes.
An existing plan artifact is evaluated (e.g. a repository-wide review) without any current edit, and its name is checked against the registered grammar.
doesNotFire: Files or records that do not play the plan-artifact role (e.g. application source code).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete artifact kinds that play the plan-artifact role; these define the rule's scope ('a planner artifact' in the Bun text).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance or planning doc; the list is not exhaustive

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file or record is assigned to the plan-artifact role — the observer the activation fact needs and that does not exist yet.
profileRequirements.bunValue: Requires an observer that classifies a file or record as a planner artifact; no such classifier exists yet.

bunOnly.text: Possible findings for an in-scope planner artifact: artifact_name_not_urn_based, artifact_name_not_matching_registered_grammar, artifact_urn_changed (requires the prior URN for comparison).
bunOnly.reason: Finding ids of this one rule's Bun checker are realization details; the core's verification describes the three violation classes, the prior-URN requirement and the satisfied-not-inapplicable semantics generically.

classification.note: Core keeps the role-level 'a plan artifact'; the concrete kind examples (plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance, planning doc; non-exhaustive) are the profile's plan-artifact kinds and are not repeated in the core.

Role-level gate: the file kind plays the plan-artifact role (Bun value 'planner_artifact'); observability needs_new_observer kept. The note's sole-gate and findings-are-not-prerequisites semantics go to core verification; recognizing the kind uses the profile's kinds and role assignment.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral already: it speaks of plan artifacts, URNs and a registered grammar, with no Bun-specific mechanics, so the core keeps the Bun wording nearly verbatim (only 'planner artifact' is rendered as the plan-artifact role). Residual concrete data carried by the profile: the plan-artifact kinds (roles.plan_artifact.kinds) and how a file is recognized as one (roles.assignment; the needed observer does not exist yet). The registered grammar itself is deliberately left as an unresolved repository-level reference: bun.json names only 'the repository's registered naming grammar' and supplies no concrete per-kind URN shapes and no declaration syntax, so no urn.* profile entries are claimed and no new vocabulary key is proposed (the existing urn.<artifact> keys describe concrete shapes that bun.json does not provide; inventing them would misrepresent the source). The Bun checker's finding ids are bunOnly. 'Product capability' and 'DESIRED OUTCOME' are ATDD artifact kinds kept as profile data, not core vocabulary.
